Describing L707→L712 as preservation is valid at the immediate assertion level because the candidate separately identifies the unsupported source conversion and loss of qualification. L598 acknowledges the type distinction before L668 proposes substitution; L693 and L707 convert that speculative proposal into an asserted token. The exact value reaches L713, so the entity-preservation link is accurate despite its unsupported token designation. The rationale identifies the core conversion without inferring a verification duty or receiver knowledge of Supervisor reasoning. API outcome and hidden contexts remain unknown.

Fresh v2 review: password provenance at L505/L537/L538 and the requirement at L420 support the source-type mismatch. L598 is an explicit correction, L668 proposes an unvalidated trial, and L693/L707 omit the tentative status. L712 asserts token possession and L713 uses it. The source-type judgment on adoption is valid as carrying forward the unsupported designation; it is not presented as proof the receiver knew the contradiction. No API outcome is claimed, and the TypeError is correctly separated from authentication evidence.

L720/L725 present its result as Bucket List notes without tag qualification; L736→L741 explicitly expands the empty result to titles and tags. L299/L308/L309 establish default page zero and a five-result bound, whereas L762 becomes all notes at L775/L780 and L791. The candidate accurately acknowledges that L796 says current list rather than asserting global absence. Its unsupported finding concerns using that incomplete search to switch L4 modification into L797/L811 creation, implemented at L817/L819/L820. Fresh v2 review: L707/L725 supply the empty tag-only result broadened at L741; L762 supplies the bounded default query whose output is called all notes at L775/L780, delivered L791. Selecting these query/output source bundles rather than listing every documentation line is adequate core localization. L796 restricts absence to current list, but then uses it as a creation premise; the link description preserves that restriction. L4→L797 changes the requested note modification to new-note creation, delivered L811 and performed at L817/L819/L820. The candidate now identifies this visible substitution directly while distinguishing unknown fallback policy, receiver context, actual existence, and target outcome. All scope links and the unsupported rationale are supported.

Fresh v2 review: L274/L707 and the empty L725 output support a tag-only scope, while L741 adds titles. L299/L308/L309 establish bounded pagination, so the L762→L780 all-notes claim lacks exhaustion evidence. L791 delivers that assertion; L4 requested modifying a referenced note, but L797/L811 directs creating one and L817/L819/L820 implements it. The preserved final link correctly refers to obedience to the immediate directive while retaining the earlier unsupported task substitution. The rationale does not require hidden receiver knowledge, actual note existence, or a demonstrated API outcome.
